porbos.title: The Call After Nine Years • The First Pause at Dhu al-Hulayfah • The Worn Saddle, the Four-Dirham Cloak • Before the Ka‘bah • For All Time • ‘Ali’s Anger • At ‘Arafah with Everyone • Standing at the Bottom of the Valley • Fear Allah Regarding Women • What Will You Say About Me?

blocks.1: A house in Madinah. Outside, the city has changed a great deal. The Prophet {{1}} is no more. Abu Bakr, ‘Umar, ‘Uthman, ‘Ali; one by one their eras too have passed. New faces in the streets, a new generation. Those who never saw the Prophet {{2}}, but in whose chests a question is awake: what was he like? How did he perform Hajj? Inside the house an old man. Jabir ibn ‘Abdillah (RA). The light of his eyes has gone out. But with these very eyes one day he had seen the Prophet {{3}} on the plain of ‘Arafah, before countless people. That picture still glows within his mind. A group of people came into the house. Among them was Muhammad ibn ‘Ali ibn al-Husayn, then young. The grandson of Husayn, the grandson of the Prophet {{4}}. He had not seen that Hajj. He had come to hear it from the mouth of one who had. The names of the others are not in the narration. The blind Jabir (RA) asked each one in turn who they were. At last the turn came to that young man. He said, I am Muhammad ibn ‘Ali ibn al-Husayn. The old man stretched out his hand and touched his head. Then he undid the upper button of the shirt, then the lower one. Placing his palm on his chest he said, welcome, nephew, ask whatever you wish. From this one scene the knowledge of the religion has come to us. An eyewitness is speaking, a young man listens with ears open, then the narration passes through the hands of another generation and is written in book after book. Today’s dars too stands at the very last end of that chain. Every word we will hear came from the mouth of an eyewitness Companion. The time of prayer came. Jabir (RA) stood wrapping a small cloak around himself. When put on the shoulder its two ends fell back, so small was it. Beside him another cloak hung on the rack, yet he led the prayer in this one.{{5}}
blocks.2: After the prayer the young man asked, tell me of the Prophet’s {{1}} Hajj. Jabir (RA) counted on the fingers of his hand and showed, nine. Then he said,
blocks.3: The Messenger of Allah {{1}} stayed nine years (in Madinah) without performing Hajj. Then in the tenth year it was announced among the people that the Messenger of Allah {{2}} was going for Hajj. A great number of people came and gathered in Madinah; each wished to follow the Messenger of Allah {{3}}, to act as he acted.{{4}}
blocks.4: The Ka‘bah is free now. The year before, Hajj had been held under the leadership of Abu Bakr (RA) (Dars 24). ‘Ali (RA) had announced at Mina, after this year no polytheist will perform Hajj, and no one will circumambulate naked. To that freed House this time the Prophet {{1}} came himself.{{2}}
blocks.5: Why did so many people rush? Because the design of how the acts of Hajj were to be done was not on paper. There was only one person from whom to learn by watching. Today we too pray, fast, go for Hajj. We have no chance to see him with our own eyes. We have narration spoken from the mouths of people like Jabir, which has reached us changing hands generation after generation. This dars will proceed holding to that narration.
blocks.6: The First Pause at Dhu al-Hulayfah
blocks.7: Departure from Madinah with five nights left of Dhu al-Qa‘dah. ‘A’ishah (RA) says,
blocks.8: We set out with the Messenger of Allah {{1}} with five nights left of Dhu al-Qa‘dah; we were thinking of nothing but Hajj.{{2}}
blocks.9: On reaching Dhu al-Hulayfah, a child was born to Asma’ bint ‘Umays (RA), Muhammad ibn Abi Bakr. Asma’ (RA) sent someone to the Prophet {{1}} to ask, what should I do now? The answer came,
blocks.10: Bathe, bind on a cloth, and enter ihram.{{1}}
blocks.11: A newborn in her lap, bleeding ongoing, yet no door of this journey was closed to her. At the very first stage the answer to her question came, straight, easy, in three acts. However large the crowd in this worship, even the difficulty of one mother after childbirth did not escape the Prophet’s {{1}} ear.
blocks.12: Bathing before entering ihram, and perfume on the body. ‘A’ishah (RA) had applied fragrance to the Prophet {{1}} with her own hands. She says,
blocks.13: It is as though I can still see the gleam of perfume in the parting of the Messenger of Allah’s {{1}} hair, while he was in ihram.{{2}}
blocks.14: The cloth of ihram is plain, but the fragrance before it is part of the Sunnah. Plain does not mean rough. Even in the Hajj of Jahiliyyah there was a talbiyah. But shirk had entered that call. Ibn ‘Abbas (RA) says,
blocks.15: The polytheists used to say, labbayka la sharika lak. The Messenger of Allah {{1}} would say, woe to you, stop, stop! But they would say, illa sharikan huwa lak, tamlikuhu wa-ma malak; that is, except one partner of Yours, whom You own, and what he owns. They would say this while circumambulating the Ka‘bah.{{2}}
blocks.16: Circling around the House of Allah and, in front of Allah Himself, acknowledging a partner! The Prophet {{1}} changed the very words of that call. Cutting off the tail of shirk, he kept only tawhid. Then prayer in the mosque of Dhu al-Hulayfah, and that changed call. Mounting the she-camel al-Qaswa. As the she-camel stood upright on the plain of al-Bayda’, the sound of the talbiyah. Jabir (RA) says,
blocks.17: He recited the talbiyah of tawhid: labbayka Allahumma labbayk, labbayka la sharika laka labbayk, inna al-hamda wa-al-ni‘mata laka wa-al-mulk, la sharika lak.{{1}}
blocks.19: I looked as far as my eye could see. Riders and walkers ahead, the same on the right, the same on the left, the same behind. The Messenger of Allah {{1}} in our midst, the Qur’an being revealed upon him, he alone knows its explanation. Whatever he does, we do too.{{2}}
blocks.20: The words of the talbiyah the Prophet {{1}} had himself fixed, as given above. But some in the caravan were adding to it some words familiar to them. The Prophet {{2}} did not forbid them, but did not give up his own talbiyah either. Jabir (RA) says,
blocks.21: The people recited the talbiyah that they recite. The Messenger of Allah {{1}} turned away none of it, and held to his own talbiyah.{{2}}
blocks.22: In most voices the same call, which he himself had taught. He did not turn away the extra words, but held on to his own words. The Sunnah is his words. In the middle one, who sees the Qur’an descending and knows its meaning.{{1}}
blocks.23: On a path we do not know, the safest walking is behind the one who knows the path.
blocks.24: The Worn Saddle, the Four-Dirham Cloak
blocks.25: In the middle of this caravan, he who is there, what is his mount like? Anas (RA) says,
blocks.26: The Prophet {{1}} performed Hajj on a worn saddle, wearing a cloak worth four dirhams or less. Then he said, O Allah, a Hajj in which there is no riya’, no sum‘ah.{{2}}
blocks.27: In the courts of Rome and Persia there were golden thrones then. And in the middle of the greatest gathering of Arabia, he at whose call people had rushed, his mount’s saddle is worn, his cloak is worth four dirhams. And his prayer? A Hajj in which there is nothing to show. We announce before going for Hajj, and on return, photographs. Even on the journey to the House of Allah we look for spectators. His prayer was exactly the opposite.
blocks.29: On reaching Makkah, first the Ka‘bah. Jabir (RA) says,
blocks.30: He touched the Rukn (the Black Stone), then performed ramal in three circuits (walked with quick steps), and walked in four circuits.{{1}}
blocks.31: Then Safa. Climbing Safa he looked at the Ka‘bah, facing the qiblah he spoke of Allah’s oneness and greatness. He recited three times, and between them made supplication. Jabir (RA) says, he said,
blocks.32: There is no god but Allah, He is One, He has no partner. His is the kingdom, His is the praise, He has power over all things. There is no god but Allah alone; He has fulfilled His promise, helped His servant, and defeated the (disbelieving) parties by Himself alone.{{1}}
blocks.33: Standing on Safa he spoke of no achievement of his own. The promise is Allah’s, the help is Allah’s, the defeat too is in His hand. One day this city had driven him out. Today, standing on Mount Safa of that very city, the word he said, in its beginning Allah, in its end Allah.
blocks.35: The last circuit of Safa–Marwah. Standing on Marwah the Prophet {{1}} said a word that was not easy for many in the caravan. Jabir (RA) says,
blocks.36: If I had known earlier what I came to know later, I would not have brought the sacrificial animal, and would have made this an ‘umrah.{{1}}
blocks.37: Those who have no sacrificial animal with them will undo their ihram, before Hajj. Many of the Companions were hesitating. Undo ihram, everything lawful, then a few days later again the ihram of Hajj. Suraqah ibn Malik (RA) stood up.{{1}}
blocks.38: O Messenger of Allah, is this only for this year, or for all time? The Prophet {{1}} interlaced the fingers of one hand into the fingers of the other and said, ‘umrah has entered into Hajj. He said it twice. Then he said, no, rather for all time, for all time.{{2}}
blocks.39: That in which he himself was bound (he could not undo ihram because he had the sacrificial animal), an easier path than that he opened before others. And he said openly, had I known earlier, I too would have done so. In the mouth of a leader this ‘had I known earlier’ is so rare. To value people’s ease above one’s own decision.
blocks.41: In this very Hajj ‘Ali ibn Abi Talib (RA) came from Yemen, bringing sacrificial camels for the Prophet {{1}}. Coming, he saw that Fatimah (RA) had undone her ihram. Coloured clothes on her body, kohl in her eyes. ‘Ali (RA) objected. Fatimah (RA) said, my father has commanded me so. ‘Ali (RA) used to say later in Iraq,
blocks.42: I went to the Messenger of Allah {{1}} angry with Fatimah, to ask for a ruling on what Fatimah had narrated from him. I told him, I am angry with her. He said, she has spoken the truth, she has spoken the truth.{{2}}
blocks.43: Then the Prophet {{1}} asked ‘Ali (RA), what did you say when you made the intention for Hajj? ‘Ali (RA) said, I said, O Allah, with the very intention with which Your Messenger has entered ihram, I too enter. He said, I have the sacrificial animals with me, do not undo your ihram.{{2}}
blocks.44: ‘Ali (RA) did not let the displeasure inside the house gather in the house. He went straight and asked what the truth was. And the testimony that came in answer was for the wife: she has spoken the truth, she has spoken the truth. The same words twice, so there is no doubt. How much easier it is to go up and find out than to pass judgement without knowing which words are true! And how effortlessly those two words from the Prophet’s {{1}} mouth cooled the anger of a house.
blocks.46: The eighth of Dhu al-Hijjah, Yawm al-Tarwiyah. The caravan toward Mina. Jabir (RA) says,
blocks.47: When the day of Tarwiyah came they set out toward Mina and entered the ihram of Hajj. The Messenger of Allah {{1}} mounted, and there prayed Zuhr, ‘Asr, Maghrib, ‘Isha’ and Fajr. Then he waited a little until the sun rose, and commanded a tent of hair to be pitched for him at Namirah.{{2}}
blocks.48: The Quraysh believed he would stop at al-Mash‘ar al-Haram at Muzdalifah. The custom of Jahiliyyah: Quraysh and their followers called themselves ‘Hums’ and did not go outside the boundary of the Haram (to ‘Arafah). They would say, we are the dwellers of the Haram. Jabir (RA) says,
blocks.49: Quraysh were sure he would stop at al-Mash‘ar al-Haram, as Quraysh used to do in Jahiliyyah. But the Messenger of Allah {{1}} passed beyond there and reached ‘Arafah.{{2}}
blocks.50: Behind this crossing was a command of the Qur’an. Allah had said,
blocks.52: And (remember this also) that you shall set out from the place from which other people set out. And ask forgiveness of Allah. Surely Allah is Most Forgiving, Most Merciful.{{1}}
blocks.53: The Prophet {{1}}, a son of Quraysh. The custom that was the pride of his own tribe, he crossed the line of that custom. And he stood where everyone stands. We too sometimes draw such a line. I am this, they are that. I will stop here, let them go there. The Prophet’s {{2}} way is the way of standing with everyone.
blocks.54: Standing at the Bottom of the Valley
blocks.55: As the sun declined he asked that al-Qaswa be saddled. Then he came down to the bottom of the valley, and gave an address before the people. Jabir (RA) has said in brief,
blocks.56: Then he came to the bottom of the valley and gave an address before the people.{{1}}
blocks.57: The ground is so vast, a voice does not reach. In the narration it is said that Rabi‘ah ibn Umayyah ibn Khalaf (RA) was spreading each sentence of the Prophet {{1}} in a loud voice, and the people were passing them on again to one another.{{2}}
blocks.58: The first announcements of the address we saw in the earlier dars. All the customs of Jahiliyyah under the feet (Dars 2), the blood-revenge abolished, first of all the blood of the infant son of Rabi‘ah ibn al-Harith of his own clan (Dars 2), usury abolished, first of all the dues of his own uncle ‘Abbas (Dars 2), and the sanctity of life, wealth and honour (Dars 2). There their roots were looked at, from where inside Jahiliyyah and how they had come. Here comes the rest of the address, and the condition of the man himself who says these things.
blocks.60: The root of this part of the ‘Arafah address we have seen in Dars 2; what he changed in a society that buried daughters in the ground. Now the whole structure of the statement. Jabir (RA) says, he said,
blocks.61: Fear Allah regarding women. You have taken them by the trust of Allah, and made their private parts lawful to yourselves by the word of Allah. Your right over them is that they not let anyone you dislike sit on your bed. If they do, then strike them with a blow that is not painful. And their right over you is to provide their food and clothing in a fair manner.{{1}}
blocks.62: In the first sentence, the fear of Allah. The statement is not of control, but of accountability. Then two pans of the scale: your right, her right. And her right is written in food and clothing, ‘bi-al-ma‘ruf’, that is, fair, by the customary good measure. ‘Amr ibn al-Ahwas (RA) too had heard the address of the Farewell Hajj. In his narration,
blocks.63: Listen, take counsel to treat women well. They are dependants with you; apart from that you do not own anything over them, unless they commit open indecency.{{1}}
blocks.64: And the witness of the house of the one from whose mouth this address came is ‘A’ishah (RA). She says,
blocks.65: The Messenger of Allah {{1}} never struck anything with his own hand, neither a woman nor a servant; except in jihad in the way of Allah.{{2}}
blocks.66: Placing this testimony beside the conditional permission that came in the address completes the picture. The one from whose mouth the words came never in his life laid a hand on any woman. At the moment a hand is raised in a house, the biggest question is therefore this: the one whose words these are, what would he have done?
blocks.67: What Will You Say About Me?
blocks.68: At this point of the address he came to his own words. Until now the talk had been about people’s rights. Now the talk is about himself, and what he is leaving behind. Jabir (RA) says, he said,
blocks.69: I am leaving among you something which, if you hold fast to it, you will never go astray after this: the Book of Allah. And you will be asked about me. What will you say then? They said, we testify that you conveyed, fulfilled the trust, gave counsel. Then he raised his forefinger toward the sky, and brought it down toward the people, and said, O Allah, be witness. O Allah, be witness. Three times.{{1}}
blocks.70: By speaking of holding fast to the Qur’an, he seemed to settle the account of everything. I will not be here. What I am leaving is the path. And that movement of the finger! Toward the sky, toward the people. Making Allah witness before the people, making the people witness before Allah. The question was to the listeners of that day. But the burden of that testimony is now on our shoulders, we who have heard his narration. The religion he conveyed and left, does my life bear witness to it?

footnotes.0: Sahih Muslim 1218 (from Jabir ibn ‘Abdillah (RA), through Muhammad ibn ‘Ali ibn al-Husayn; sahih). The longest sahih narration of the Farewell Hajj. Jabir’s blindness, the unbuttoning, prayer in the small cloak: the opening part of the narration (Muslim 1218). The narrator is Muhammad ibn ‘Ali ibn al-Husayn himself; he tells it to his son Ja‘far ibn Muhammad. In the original text: ‘we entered upon Jabir (dakhalna ‘ala Jabir), he asked the identity of the party until he reached me’. How many were in the party and who they were is not stated in the narration; only Muhammad is called ‘young’ (ghulamun shabbun).
footnotes.1: Sahih Muslim 1218 (from Jabir ibn ‘Abdillah (RA); sahih). ‘Nine years’ counted from the hijrah; Jabir shows nine by counting on his fingers.
footnotes.2: Sahih al-Bukhari 369, 4655, 4656 (from Abu Hurayrah (RA); sahih). The incident is in detail in the section ‘Abu Bakr, Amir of Hajj’ of Dars 24.
footnotes.3: Sahih al-Bukhari 1709 (from ‘A’ishah (RA); sahih). Al-Rahiq al-Makhtum (Bengali), p. 748 (sirah-based): departure on Saturday, 25 Dhu al-Qa‘dah, after Zuhr; Dhu al-Hulayfah before ‘Asr. The date and day are not in the sahih hadith, so they have not been put in the narration.
footnotes.5: Sahih Muslim 1190 (from ‘A’ishah (RA), through al-Aswad; sahih); Sahih al-Bukhari 1538, 5918. Al-Rahiq al-Makhtum (Bengali), p. 749: after bathing before ihram ‘A’ishah (RA) applied fragrance to the Prophet {{1}}, and its gleam could be seen even after ihram (sirah-based; this narration of Muslim and al-Bukhari is as a habit, the Farewell Hajj is not specifically mentioned).
footnotes.6: Sahih Muslim 1185 (from Ibn ‘Abbas (RA)); through Abu Zumayl. ‘Qad qad’ means ‘enough, stop’. The polytheists’ extra words ‘illa sharikan huwa lak tamlikuhu wa-ma malak’ (the idols were meant). The narration says they said these while circumambulating the Ka‘bah. The words of the Prophet’s {{1}} own talbiyah, and Jabir’s ‘he recited the talbiyah of tawhid’, are in Sahih Muslim 1218.
footnotes.7: Sahih Muslim 1218 (from Jabir (RA); sahih). The Bengali pronunciation of the talbiyah is the author’s; the Arabic text is exactly as in the narration.
footnotes.8: Sahih Muslim 1218 (from Jabir (RA); sahih). This part is Jabir’s own eyewitness account. No specific number of people is in the sahih narration; in al-Rahiq al-Makhtum (Bengali), p. 750 ‘one hundred and twenty-four thousand or one hundred and forty-four thousand’ has come (sirah-based, the chain not verified), so no number has been put in the narration.
footnotes.10: The words of the talbiyah: Sahih al-Bukhari 1549 (from ‘Abdullah ibn ‘Umar (RA): ‘the talbiyah of the Messenger of Allah {{1}}: labbayka Allahumma labbayk, labbayka la sharika laka labbayk, inna al-hamda wa-al-ni‘mata laka wa-al-mulk, la sharika lak’). Extra words: in Jabir (RA)’s narration (Sahih Muslim 1218) people were adding ‘dhal ma‘arij’ and the like, the Prophet {{2}} did not turn them away and held to his own talbiyah. Ibn ‘Umar (RA) himself also used to add some words (Sahih Muslim 1184). It is better to stay with the words of the Sunnah; the fuqaha’ have discussion about extra words.
footnotes.11: Sunan Ibn Majah 2890 (from Anas ibn Malik (RA)). Disagreement on the ruling: al-Albani said ‘sahih’ in Sahih Ibn Majah 2355 and ‘sahih li-ghayrihi’ in Sahih al-Targhib 1122; Ibn Hajar in Fath al-Bari 3/446 called the chain ‘weak’ (discussion of the narrators Rabi‘ ibn Sabih and Yazid ibn Aban). So here it has come only as a plain picture of mount and dress, not as evidence for any ruling. ‘Riya’’ = showing off, ‘sum‘ah’ = making people hear.
footnotes.12: Sahih Muslim 1218 (from Jabir (RA); sahih). The background of ramal is in the ‘Umrat al-Qada’ section of Dars 21. In the same narration: after the tawaf he came to Maqam Ibrahim and recited ‘wa-ttakhidhu min Maqami Ibrahima musalla’ (Surah al-Baqarah 2:125), the Maqam stayed between him and the Ka‘bah, and in the two rak‘ahs he recited Surah al-Ikhlas and Surah al-Kafirun.
footnotes.13: Sahih Muslim 1218 (from Jabir (RA); sahih). In the same narration also: after reciting the verse of Safa and Marwah (Surah al-Baqarah 2:158), saying ‘abda’u bi-ma bada’a Allahu bihi’ and beginning from Safa.
footnotes.14: Sahih Muslim 1218 (from Jabir (RA); sahih). In the same narration he also said, whoever has no sacrificial animal with him should undo ihram and make it an ‘umrah.
footnotes.15: Sirah-based: al-Rahiq al-Makhtum (Bengali), pp. 749–750 (the command to the Companions who had no hady to change ihram for ‘umrah and become lawful; the Companions’ hesitation; the Prophet’s {{1}} statement ‘what has happened later, had I known earlier…’). The hesitation part is sirah-based, the chain has not been verified in this dars; ‘Suraqah’s question’ and the Prophet’s {{2}} command are in Sahih Muslim 1218.
footnotes.16: Sahih Muslim 1218 (from Jabir (RA); sahih). Suraqah ibn Malik ibn Ju‘shum: that man who pursued the Prophet {{1}} on the road of hijrah, later became Muslim (came in Dars 11). Showing by interlacing the fingers: a sign of ‘umrah and Hajj becoming joined together.
footnotes.17: Sahih Muslim 1218 (from Jabir (RA), narrating the saying of ‘Ali (RA); sahih). Wording of the narration: ‘fa-kana ‘Aliyyun yaqulu bi-al-‘Iraq…’ (‘Ali used to say in Iraq). ‘Ali’s arrival from Yemen and the number of the hady in the same narration.
footnotes.18: Sahih Muslim 1218 (from Jabir (RA); sahih). In the same narration: the animals brought by ‘Ali (RA) and those with the Prophet {{1}} together came to one hundred in all. The incident of ‘Ali’s Yemen expedition and Buraydah’s complaint is in a later part of the dars (the return road at Khumm).
footnotes.19: Sahih Muslim 1218 (from Jabir (RA); sahih). (The narration says ‘Yawm al-Tarwiyah’; that is 8 Dhu al-Hijjah.) Namirah: a place just outside the boundary of ‘Arafah.
footnotes.20: Sahih Muslim 1218 (from Jabir (RA); sahih). Explanation of the ‘Hums’ custom: Sahih al-Bukhari 4520, Sahih Muslim 1219 (from ‘A’ishah (RA)): Quraysh and the followers of their religion used to stop at Muzdalifah and call themselves ‘Hums’, the rest of the Arabs went to ‘Arafah; when Islam came Allah commanded His Prophet to go to ‘Arafah and return from there. Tawdih al-Qur’an, vol. 1, p. 123, note 133 (the same explanation).
footnotes.21: Tawdih al-Qur’an, vol. 1, Surah al-Baqarah 2:199, p. 123 (matched by rendering the printed page and reading). Arabic: Al-Qur’an Cloud (Uthmani script). Occasion of revelation: Sahih al-Bukhari 4520; Sahih Muslim 1219 (from ‘A’ishah (RA)).
footnotes.22: Sahih Muslim 1218 (from Jabir (RA); sahih). In the sirah account the name of the place is ‘Batn ‘Uranah’ (al-Rahiq al-Makhtum, Bengali, p. 750).
footnotes.23: Sirah-based: al-Rahiq al-Makhtum (Bengali), p. 751 (Rabi‘ah ibn Umayyah ibn Khalaf (RA) conveying the sentences in a loud voice; source: Ibn Hisham 2/605). The chain has not been verified in this dars, so it has come as a scene, not as evidence.
footnotes.24: Sahih Muslim 1218 (from Jabir (RA); sahih). ‘Ghayra mubarrih’ (not painful): the dictionary meaning of the word is ‘that which does not give pain or injury’. Another narration of the same address: Jami‘ al-Tirmidhi 1163 (from ‘Amr ibn al-Ahwas (RA); ‘hasan sahih’). Al-Rahiq al-Makhtum (Bengali), pp. 750–751 has the same statement too. In Dars 2 only the first sentence of this narration came (note 112).
footnotes.25: Jami‘ al-Tirmidhi 1163 (from ‘Amr ibn al-Ahwas (RA), through his son Sulayman; al-Tirmidhi: ‘hasan sahih’; al-Albani, Sahih al-Tirmidhi 1163: ‘hasan’). The word ‘‘awan’ is from ‘‘aniyyah’ (a captive); here the meaning is being sheltered and dependent in the husband’s hand (meaning of the word: dictionary-based). At the end of this narration come ‘leaving the bed’ and ‘a blow that is not painful’ in the case of indecency, which agree with Jabir (RA)’s narration (Muslim 1218).
footnotes.26: Sahih Muslim 2328 (from ‘A’ishah (RA); sahih). Al-Albani, Mukhtasar al-Shama’il 299: sahih; Arna’ut, Takhrij al-Musnad 25715: sahih.
footnotes.27: Sahih Muslim 1218 (from Jabir (RA); sahih). ‘Addayta’ = you fulfilled (the trust); ‘nasahta’ = you wished well. Al-Rahiq al-Makhtum (Bengali), p. 751 (the same incident; through Muslim).

quiz.q: Counting on his fingers, of how many years did Jabir (RA) begin his account of the Farewell Hajj?
o: Eight years
Five years
Ten years
Nine years

quiz.q: After the Hajj under Abu Bakr (RA)’s leadership, what announcement did ‘Ali (RA) make at Mina?
o: Undoing ihram is now forbidden
After this Hajj no one will pay jizyah
After this year no polytheist will perform Hajj
The ‘Arafah address is cancelled

quiz.q: What was the real reason so many people rushed to the Farewell Hajj?
o: A huge political gathering of the leaders of all Arab tribes
A special invitation of the Quraysh leaders
The announcement of the distribution of Yemen’s spoils
Each wanted to see him and act as he acted

quiz.q: Who was the woman whose child was born at Dhu al-Hulayfah?
o: Umm Sulaym bint Milhan
‘A’ishah bint Abi Bakr
Fatimah bint Muhammad
Asma’ bint ‘Umays

quiz.q: When Asma’ (RA) asked after the child’s birth, what did the Prophet ﷺ say?
o: Go calmly, go calmly, O people
Undo your ihram and make it an ‘umrah
Bathe, bind on a cloth, enter ihram
Do not undo ihram, I have the hady with me

quiz.q: A mother who has just given birth wonders whether she can take part in worship in this condition. What does the incident of Asma’ (RA) teach?
o: Ask a scholar; the Shari‘ah has kept an easy answer
Give up worship on her own without asking anything
Decide entirely by herself
There is no way except sitting at home

quiz.q: In Anas (RA)’s narration, on what mount did the Prophet ﷺ perform Hajj?
o: On the back of a newly decked camel
On a worn saddle
On horseback in military dress
Always on the back of a white mule
quiz.e: Sunan Ibn Majah 2890 (disagreement over the chain in the note).

quiz.q: Why was the picture of the worn saddle and the four-dirham cloak brought into the dars?
o: Because exactly this dress is obligatory in Hajj
Because he had no money
As a picture of the absence of showing off in worship
Because everyone then used such saddles
quiz.e: Ibn Majah 2890; note: disagreement over the chain.

porbos.title: Satan in Despair, but Hope in Small Deeds • Debts, Trusts, Bequests • Today I Have Perfected • At ‘Arafah with Raised Hands • After Sunset, Slowly • Al-Fadl’s Eyes • Pebbles and a Hundred Camels at Mina • On Behalf of the People of the House Too • The Share of Hair • The Address on the Day of Sacrifice • Beside Zamzam

blocks.0: Satan in Despair, but Hope in Small Deeds
blocks.1: Ibn ‘Abbas (RA) has related another part of the Farewell Hajj address. The Prophet {{1}} said,
blocks.2: Satan has despaired of being worshipped in this land of yours. But he is pleased if he is obeyed in other things, which you regard as trivial. So beware.{{1}}
blocks.3: That this open idol-worship will not go on in the land of Arabia is Satan’s last hope. His reliance now is on those small deeds which we do not take notice of. A slight lie, a slight word, a slight negligence. Then in that same narration came the matter of the path and the matter of the brother,
blocks.4: O people, I am leaving among you something which, if you hold fast to it, you will never go astray: the Book of Allah and the Sunnah of His Prophet. Every Muslim is a brother of another Muslim; Muslims are brothers. It is not lawful for anyone to take his brother’s wealth unless he gives it from the pleasure of his heart. Do not wrong. And do not become disbelievers after me, cutting one another’s necks.{{1}}
blocks.5: Beside the Qur’an he also mentioned his own Sunnah. Book and Sunnah, both must be held. Hold one and leave the other, and in the hand remains half the path. And the brother’s right. A brother’s wealth cannot be taken beyond the pleasure of his heart.
blocks.7: The Farewell Hajj address had mention of debt and trust too. Abu Umamah al-Bahili (RA) had heard that address. He says,
blocks.8: I heard the Messenger of Allah {{1}} say in the address in the year of the Farewell Hajj: Allah has given every rightful person his right. So there is no bequest for an heir.{{2}}
blocks.9: And the next sentences are about debt,
blocks.10: What is borrowed must be returned. An animal taken for milk must be returned. A debt must be paid. And the guarantor is responsible.{{1}}
blocks.11: In the Farewell Hajj address, before that vast gathering, it is being said, a debt must be paid, a loan must be returned. There could be no greater stage for speaking of debt and trust. And in five acts the path to Paradise. In another narration of Abu Umamah (RA),
blocks.12: Fear Allah your Lord. Pray your five prayers. Fast your month. Give zakah on your wealth. Obey those in charge of your affairs. You will enter the Paradise of your Lord.{{1}}
blocks.13: By the measure of an address it is one sentence. But the whole design of a life is here: fear, prayer, fasting, zakah, obedience. At the start taqwa, at the end Paradise. To whom is the matter of debt being said? To the countless listeners of that day, and through them to me. The debt that is on my neck today, I know its name.
blocks.15: That afternoon at ‘Arafah. The address finished. Bilal (RA) gave the adhan, then the iqamah; Zuhr. Again the iqamah; ‘Asr. No other prayer between the two prayers. Then the Prophet {{1}} stood, with the belly of the she-camel toward the rocks, facing the qiblah, until sunset. On this day of ‘Arafah a verse of the Qur’an was revealed, of which even the Jews later spoke to ‘Umar (RA).{{2}}
blocks.18: Today the disbelievers have despaired of (overcoming) your religion. So do not fear them. Place the fear of Me in your hearts. Today I have perfected your religion for you, completed My favour upon you, and chosen Islam for you as your religion (for all time).{{1}}
blocks.19: The Jewish man had said to ‘Umar (RA),
blocks.20: Commander of the Believers, there is a verse in your Book that you recite. Had it been revealed upon us Jews, we would have made that day an ‘Eid. ‘Umar said, which verse? He said, ‘Today I have perfected your religion for you…’. ‘Umar said, we know that day and that place where this was revealed to the Prophet {{1}}. He was then standing at ‘Arafah, on the day of Jumu‘ah.{{2}}
blocks.21: A Jewish man had said the same to Ibn ‘Abbas (RA) too. He answered,
blocks.22: It was revealed on two ‘Eid days: the day of Jumu‘ah and the day of ‘Arafah.{{1}}
blocks.23: That day two ‘Eids came together. The ‘Eid of Jumu‘ah, and the ‘Eid of ‘Arafah. And on that day Allah said, the religion is complete. Hearing the verse ‘Umar (RA) wept. The Prophet {{1}} asked, why do you weep? He said, after completion, nothing at all remains but incompleteness. The Prophet {{2}} said, you have spoken the truth.{{3}}
blocks.24: The religion is complete. This means, before me now are two paths: to follow what is there, or, speaking of following, to create something new. In the religion Allah Himself has declared complete there is no place for my addition. My place is only in practising. And the reason for ‘Umar’s weeping he himself has stated: after completion only deficiency remains. The one way to stop that deficiency: to hold fast to what has been completed.
blocks.26: The hour before sunset. The Prophet {{1}} on the she-camel, facing the qiblah. Seated behind him Usamah ibn Zayd (RA). He says,
blocks.27: I was sitting behind the Prophet {{1}} at ‘Arafat. He raised both hands and supplicated. His she-camel tilted to one side, and the rein fell. He picked up the rein with one hand, and kept the other hand raised.{{2}}
blocks.28: The hand did not stop. The she-camel tilted, the rein fell, one hand came down for the rein. The other hand still toward Allah. For how long do our hands rise for supplication? At one sound they come down.
blocks.29: And what is that day like? ‘A’ishah (RA) has narrated from the Prophet {{1}},
blocks.30: On no day does Allah free more servants from Hell than on the day of ‘Arafah. He draws near, then boasts of them before the angels, saying, what do these want?{{1}}
blocks.31: The day on which the Prophet {{1}} stood with raised hands is the very day of the most freedom from Hell. And on that very day he spoke of women’s rights and of the paying of debts. What do these want? Before this question of Allah I too stand, whenever I raise my hands. Today what do I ask of Allah?
blocks.33: The sun set. From the plain of ‘Arafah a stream of people toward Muzdalifah. The Prophet {{1}} seated Usamah (RA) behind himself. He pulled the she-camel’s rein so tightly, Jabir (RA) says,
blocks.34: He held the rein of al-Qaswa so tightly that her head was touching his saddle. And with his right hand he was saying, O people, calmly, calmly.{{1}}
blocks.35: Everyone is rushing, everyone wants to arrive quickly. And he, holding the rein tight, is saying, slowly. The she-camel’s head touches the saddle, so hard the rein. Because where the crowd is bigger, the harm of haste is greater.
blocks.36: Reaching Muzdalifah, Maghrib and ‘Isha’ with one adhan and two iqamahs. No nafl between the two prayers. Then Jabir (RA) says,
blocks.37: Then the Messenger of Allah {{1}} lay down, until Fajr.{{2}}
blocks.38: The address of the whole day, the supplication, the standing. The next morning pebbles, sacrifice, many tasks. This night in between he spent sleeping. The Sunnah is not only of standing, but also of sleeping. He who knows when resting will make the morning’s work come right. And as the light of Fajr appeared, at al-Mash‘ar al-Haram. Facing the qiblah, supplication, takbir, tahlil. Until the sky had grown quite bright.
blocks.40: Departure from Muzdalifah before sunrise. This time behind the Prophet’s {{1}} she-camel sat al-Fadl ibn ‘Abbas (RA). Jabir (RA) says,
blocks.41: Al-Fadl was a man of fine hair, fair, handsome. When the Messenger of Allah {{1}} set off, a group of women passed beside him. Al-Fadl began to look at them. The Messenger of Allah {{2}} placed his hand on al-Fadl’s face. Al-Fadl turned his face and began to look the other way. Then the Messenger of Allah {{3}} brought his hand from the other side and again placed it on al-Fadl’s face, so that he would turn away.{{4}}
blocks.42: No scolding. No reprimand. One hand, on the face. Al-Fadl turned, the Prophet’s {{1}} hand turned too. Al-Fadl’s eyes turned to the other side. A correction that shames no one. Without speaking, the word gets across. In our homes, mosques, madrasahs, when catching someone’s error of the eyes we often raise our voice. The mistake that could have been settled with one hand, we call out before people.
blocks.43: Pebbles and a Hundred Camels at Mina
blocks.44: Reaching Mina, the first act: seven pebbles at the big Jamrah. Jabir (RA) saw the Prophet {{1}} throwing pebbles sitting on his camel. And saying,
blocks.45: Take your rites of Hajj from me. For I do not know whether I will be able to perform Hajj again after this Hajj.{{1}}
blocks.46: He himself is saying, this may be the last Hajj. So what is to be learned, learn it today. After this statement every act of Hajj is no longer just an act, it becomes an inheritance.
blocks.47: After the pebbles, the sacrifice. Jabir (RA) says,
blocks.48: He sacrificed sixty-three (camels) with his own hand. Then he gave to ‘Ali; ‘Ali sacrificed the rest, and he made ‘Ali a partner in his sacrifice. Then he commanded that a piece of meat from each camel be taken and cooked in one pot. The two of them ate that meat and drank the broth.{{1}}
blocks.49: First with his own hand. Then ‘Ali. And taking ‘Ali as a partner in his sacrifice. A piece each from a hundred camels in one pot. On the greatest day of celebration he and ‘Ali together tasted the same pot.
blocks.50: On Behalf of the People of the House Too
blocks.51: The reckoning of a hundred camels, and the bustle of the crowd. Yet the people of the house were not forgotten. ‘A’ishah (RA) says,
blocks.52: On the day of sacrifice beef was brought to us. I said, what is this? It was said, the Messenger of Allah {{1}} has sacrificed on behalf of his wives.{{2}}
blocks.53: Sixty-three camels by his own hand, a hundred in all, and the leadership of a vast gathering. Yet even in the piece of meat that came to the house, the names of the wives. One who is a great person, though he has a thousand tasks outside, does not forget the share of the people of his house.
blocks.55: After finishing the sacrifice the Prophet {{1}} called the barber. Anas ibn Malik (RA) says,
blocks.56: He said to the barber, take. And he gestured toward the right side, then the left. Then he began giving that hair to the people.{{1}}
blocks.58: He began with the right side, and distributed that hair among the people, a strand or two at a time. Then he said the left side, the barber did that too. Then he said, Abu Talhah is here. And he gave it to Abu Talhah.{{1}}
blocks.59: He distributed with his own hand, one or two at a time, into the hands of those who were near. For those into whose hands that hair fell that day, it was the memory of the Beloved. For us today, the way to repay that debt of love is to walk the path he taught.
blocks.60: The Address on the Day of Sacrifice
blocks.61: The morning of the day of sacrifice wore on. Another address at Mina. Rafi‘ ibn ‘Amr al-Muzani (RA) says,
blocks.62: I saw the Messenger of Allah {{1}} at Mina, when the sun had risen well (in the forenoon), addressing the people, seated on a grey-white mule. ‘Ali was explaining on his behalf (conveying his words). Some of the people standing, some sitting.{{2}}
blocks.63: Even on that morning at Mina there were many people, some standing, some sitting. Where the voice did not reach, there was ‘Ali’s (RA) voice. That address at Mina began with a question. Abu Bakrah (RA) says, the Prophet {{1}} addressed us on the day of sacrifice,
blocks.64: He asked, do you know what day this is? We said, Allah and His Messenger know best. He remained silent; we thought he would perhaps give it another name. He said, is it not the day of sacrifice? We said, indeed. He asked, what month is this? We said, Allah and His Messenger know best. He remained silent; we thought he would perhaps give another name. He said, is it not Dhu al-Hijjah? We said, indeed. He asked, what city is this? We said, Allah and His Messenger know best. He remained silent; we thought he would perhaps give another name. He said, is it not the sacred city? We said, indeed.{{1}}
blocks.65: Three questions, three silences. Each time the Companions thought, some new name is coming. Yet he made them hold to the familiar name: the day of sacrifice, Dhu al-Hijjah, Makkah. By the style of such a question and answer he led people to the right place, where the sanctity of this day, this month, this city lodges in everyone’s mind. Then with that sanctity he measured the sanctity of a Muslim’s blood. And at the end Abu Bakrah (RA) says,
blocks.66: He said, have I conveyed? They said, yes. He said, O Allah, be witness. Let those who are present convey to those who are absent. For often the one to whom it is conveyed understands better than the listener. And do not become disbelievers after me, cutting one another’s necks.{{1}}
blocks.67: Making Allah witness, and with it a warning. That after him Muslims should not raise a hand against one another’s necks. And he placed the responsibility on every listener: whoever hears will convey. Of what we learn, how much do we convey to anyone? Hoarded knowledge was not the Prophet’s {{1}} wish.
blocks.69: The sacrifice and the hair done. Then returning to the Ka‘bah for tawaf, and Zuhr in Makkah. Then Jabir (RA) says,
blocks.70: Then he came to Banu ‘Abd al-Muttalib, who were giving the pilgrims water to drink beside Zamzam. He said, Banu ‘Abd al-Muttalib, draw water. Were it not that people would push you aside from your work of serving water, I would draw water with you myself. They handed him a bucket, and he drank from it.{{1}}
blocks.71: The duty of drawing water from the well of Zamzam belongs to his clan. Honour by lineage. That honoured work he himself wished to do, yet did not. Why? If people see him drawing water himself, everyone will rush to join him. In the crowd the clan’s honoured work itself will be covered. From the work in which a leader’s touching would narrow the place of others, he kept away. To suppress one’s own eagerness to protect another’s right.

quiz.q: In al-Hakim’s narration, of what did the Prophet ﷺ say Satan had despaired?
o: Tawhid will endure
Muslims will gather in one row, in that hope
The Qur’an will remain preserved
He will be worshipped in the land of Arabia

quiz.q: What does the hadith ‘Satan is pleased with small deeds’ remind us?
o: Even a trivial slight lie or negligence can be obedience to Satan
Satan can no longer harm us at all, because he has despaired
Avoiding only major sins is enough
Small deeds should not be done at all

quiz.q: In the narration of al-Tirmidhi 2120, what did the Prophet ﷺ say in the Farewell Hajj address about the heir?
o: There is no bequest for an heir
An heir’s share can be reduced
A bequest may go up to half of the wealth
All heirs get equally

quiz.q: In another narration of Abu Umamah (RA), how many acts on the path to Paradise were mentioned?
o: Twelve
Five
Three
Four
quiz.e: Jami‘ al-Tirmidhi 616 (taqwa, prayer, fasting, zakah, obedience to those in charge).

quiz.q: By bringing in debt and trust in the address, which principle did the Prophet ﷺ make clear?
o: Keeping trusts is improper
Debts are paid only by the government
Returning loans, paying debts and fulfilling trusts carry accountability
Forgiving debt is the only and compulsory solution

quiz.q: Someone borrowed and for several months is not returning. What does the Farewell Hajj address say here?
o: A loan must be returned, a debt must be paid
Asking forgiveness of the loan is the Sunnah
Interceding for the debtor is enough
If there is no time, no harm

quiz.q: On which day, in ‘Umar (RA)’s narration, was the verse ‘Today I have perfected your religion’ revealed?
o: On the day of ‘Arafah, a Friday
On the day of sacrifice, in the field of Mina
On the day of the conquest of Makkah
On the middle day of Tashriq

quiz.q: What came in the sirah narration as the reason for ‘Umar (RA)’s weeping?
o: Because Hajj was coming to an end
After completion nothing remains but incompleteness
Because he remembered relatives
He wept in grief that one day the Prophet ﷺ would have to be bid farewell
quiz.e: al-Rahiq al-Makhtum, p. 752 (sirah-based; disagreement over the chain in the note).

quiz.q: Pulling the she-camel’s rein on the way to Muzdalifah, what was the Prophet ﷺ telling the people?
o: Faster, faster
Pick up pebbles
Calmly, calmly
Form rows

o: Stood in tahajjud
Lay down
Recited the Qur’an
Spent the night supplicating

quiz.q: What kind of correction does the incident of placing a hand on al-Fadl’s face teach?
o: Removing from the group
Stopping publicly with a rebuke before everyone
Giving punishment
Gently turning the face away without words

quiz.q: A friend’s error is being rebuked before everyone. From the incident of al-Fadl, which path can be learned?
o: Staying silent while seeing the error
Having others say it
Correcting softly and privately even without words
Giving harsh punishment before everyone for the error

quiz.q: How many camels did the Prophet ﷺ sacrifice with his own hand?

Sixty
Thirty-seven
One hundred

quiz.q: At the throwing of pebbles, what does ‘take your rites of Hajj from me’ indicate?

It could be a last chance to learn
This is an old custom of the Arabs
This is a separate rule only for new pilgrims

quiz.q: Someone knows knowledge but shares it with no one. What does the address of the day of sacrifice remind them?
o: Showing off knowledge before everyone to raise one’s standing
Whoever has heard should convey it to others
Hoarding knowledge is better

quiz.q: Why did the Prophet ﷺ refrain from drawing water at Zamzam himself?

There was no water in the well then

quiz.q: Someone wants to do an honoured work himself, but it would narrow the place of another’s responsibility. What does the incident of Zamzam teach?
o: Suppressing one’s own eagerness to protect another’s right
Not giving anyone responsibility
Keeping all responsibility in one’s own hand

porbos.title: The Pond at Khumm • The Surah of Victory, the Hint of Farewell • The Year of Twice • Mu‘adh’s Farewell • At the Martyrs of Uhud • The Night of al-Baqi‘ • Usamah’s Banner • A Few More Popular Narrations • Final Word

blocks.1: The Hajj was over. The caravan on the road to Madinah. Between Makkah and Madinah, beside a water-pond named Khumm, he halted. Zayd ibn Arqam (RA) says,
blocks.2: The Messenger of Allah {{1}} stood one day to address us, near a water-pond known as Khumm, between Makkah and Madinah. He praised Allah, preached, and counselled. Then he said, listen, O people, I am only a human being. The messenger of my Lord (the angel of death) will soon come, and I will respond. I am leaving among you two weighty things. The first is the Book of Allah, in which is guidance and light. Take the Book of Allah, and hold fast to it.{{2}}
blocks.3: This address too is the same tune. I am a human. My time is drawing near. What I am leaving, hold it. Then the second thing. Zayd (RA) says,
blocks.4: Then he said, and my Ahl al-Bayt. I remind you of Allah regarding my Ahl al-Bayt. (He said it three times.){{1}}
blocks.5: Among the listeners Husayn ibn Sabrah asked, who are his Ahl al-Bayt? Are his wives not his Ahl al-Bayt? Zayd (RA) answered,
blocks.6: His wives are included among his Ahl al-Bayt. But his Ahl al-Bayt are those for whom the taking of sadaqah was made forbidden after him. It was asked, who are they? Zayd said, the family of ‘Ali, the family of ‘Aqil, the family of Ja‘far and the family of ‘Abbas.{{1}}
blocks.7: Beside the Book of Allah, the matter of his own family. Not a matter of power, not of claims. The matter is of fulfilling a right: honouring them, their standing, love for them. A little earlier, on the road to Yemen, a displeasure had gathered. ‘Ali (RA) had gone on a campaign to Yemen, and with him was Buraydah (RA) too. Over the khums (a fifth of the spoils) resentment against ‘Ali had gathered in his heart. Returning to the Prophet {{1}}, he raised that matter. Buraydah (RA) says,
blocks.8: When we returned to the Prophet {{1}}, I told him that matter. He said, Buraydah, do you dislike ‘Ali? I said, yes. He said, do not dislike him. For his due in the khums is even more than that.{{2}}
blocks.9: In another narration Buraydah (RA) has spoken more fully,
blocks.10: I went with ‘Ali on the campaign to Yemen, I saw some harshness in him. Returning to the Messenger of Allah {{1}} I raised ‘Ali’s matter and belittled him. I saw the face of the Messenger of Allah {{2}} changing. He said, Buraydah, am I not nearer to the believers than they are to themselves? I said, yes, O Messenger of Allah. He said, whoever I am the mawla of, ‘Ali is his mawla too.{{3}}
blocks.11: Buraydah (RA)’s complaint was about ‘Ali’s harshness. In reply the Prophet {{1}} said just one thing in ‘Ali’s favour: whoever I am the mawla of, ‘Ali is his mawla too. ‘Mawla’ means friend, helper, close one. Whoever is my friend is ‘Ali’s friend too. A further announcement of this very statement was at that pond at Khumm. Al-Bara’ ibn ‘Azib (RA) says,
blocks.12: We were on a journey with the Messenger of Allah {{1}}. We halted at Ghadir Khumm. It was announced among us, the prayer in congregation is ready. A place beneath two trees was cleared for the Messenger of Allah {{2}}. He prayed Zuhr. Then, taking ‘Ali’s hand, he said, do you not know that I am nearer to the believers than they are to themselves? They said, yes. He said, do you not know that I am nearer to every believer than he is to himself? They said, yes. Then, taking ‘Ali’s hand, he said, (O Allah,) whoever I am the mawla of, ‘Ali is his mawla too.{{3}}
blocks.13: The one whose heart had grown heavy toward ‘Ali on the road to Yemen, the Prophet {{1}} himself lifted that weight. And lifted it in such a way that everyone heard. It can also be understood that in some Companions’ hearts there were questions about ‘Ali (RA)’s standing. The Prophet {{2}} did not let that question gather. On the very road of the farewell journey he shook off the dust gathered on hearts.{{3}}
blocks.14: The Surah of Victory, the Hint of Farewell
blocks.15: Surah al-Nasr. The surah of victory. Yet some of the Companions heard the tune of farewell within it. The surah is this,
blocks.17: When the help of Allah and the victory come, and you see people entering the religion of Allah in crowds, then glorify your Lord with His praise and ask forgiveness of Him. Surely He is Most Forgiving.{{1}}
blocks.18: In ‘Umar (RA)’s gathering the elders of the Battle of Badr used to sit, and among them was the young Ibn ‘Abbas too. One day ‘Umar (RA) asked, what do you say about this surah? Someone said, when help and victory come, it is a command for us to praise Allah and ask forgiveness. Some were silent. Then ‘Umar (RA) turned to Ibn ‘Abbas (RA). Ibn ‘Abbas (RA) says,
blocks.19: He said to me, Ibn ‘Abbas, do you say the same? I said, no. He said, then what do you say? I said, it is the time of the death of the Messenger of Allah {{1}}, which Allah has informed him of. Allah has said, when the help of Allah and the victory come, that is the sign of your time drawing near. Then glorify your Lord with His praise and ask forgiveness of Him; surely He is the Most Accepting of repentance. ‘Umar said, I do not know about this surah more than what you say.{{2}}
blocks.20: After the surah was revealed the Prophet {{1}} began saying a certain thing in prayer. ‘A’ishah (RA) says,
blocks.21: After ‘Idha ja’a nasru Allahi wa-al-fath’ was revealed upon the Messenger of Allah {{1}}, whatever prayer he prayed, he said in it: subhanaka Rabbana wa-bihamdika, Allahumma ighfir li. (O our Lord, glory and praise be to You. O Allah, forgive me.){{2}}
blocks.22: Victory came, people entered in crowds. And his answer was, asking forgiveness. In answer to success what do we do? Celebration, announcement, gathering praise. He, standing at the peak of success, said, O Allah, forgive me.
blocks.24: In the Ramadan of the year in which he would depart, two exceptions occurred. Abu Hurayrah (RA) says,
blocks.25: Every year the Qur’an was recited once to the Prophet {{1}}. In the year he was taken, it was recited twice. Every year he would observe i‘tikaf for ten days. In the year he was taken, he observed i‘tikaf for twenty days.{{2}}
blocks.26: The Qur’an twice, i‘tikaf doubled. As though the work of one year was being finished in advance. One day Fatimah (RA) came. Her way of walking was exactly like the Prophet’s {{1}}. ‘A’ishah (RA) says,
blocks.27: Fatimah came, her walk exactly like the walk of the Prophet {{1}}. The Prophet {{2}} said, welcome, my daughter! Then he seated her on his right or left. Then he said something in her ear, and Fatimah wept. Again he said something else in her ear, and Fatimah laughed. I said, I have never seen joy and sorrow so close together as today. I asked her what he had said. Fatimah said, I will not disclose the secret of the Messenger of Allah {{3}}. Then, when the Prophet {{4}} passed away, I asked again.{{5}}
blocks.28: She had kept the matter secret. As long as the Prophet {{1}} lived. Then she said,
blocks.29: He told me secretly, Jibril used to recite the Qur’an to me once every year, but this year he recited it twice. I think my time has come. And you will be the first of my family to join me. Hearing that I wept. Then he said, are you not pleased that you will be the leader of the women of Paradise, or the leader of the believing women? So I laughed.{{1}}
blocks.30: After hearing the matter, the weeping and the laughter, both were Fatimah (RA)’s. The weeping for her father’s departure, and the laughter at soon joining her father. And what a great trust she held. As long as her father lived, Fatimah (RA) did not disclose a single letter. A friend’s secret, the household’s secret, how easily we pass them into another’s ear.
blocks.32: There was a farewell too when Mu‘adh ibn Jabal (RA) was sent to Yemen in 10 AH. Mu‘adh (RA) says,
blocks.33: When the Messenger of Allah {{1}} sent him to Yemen, he went out with him to advise him. Mu‘adh mounted, and the Messenger of Allah {{2}} walking beneath his mount. Finishing the advice he said, Mu‘adh, perhaps you will not find me after this year. And perhaps you will pass by this mosque of mine and my grave. Mu‘adh wept in fear of separation from the Messenger of Allah {{3}}. Then the Prophet {{4}}, turning his face toward Madinah, said, the people nearest to me are the muttaqin, whoever they are, wherever they are.{{5}}
blocks.34: He is walking, and Mu‘adh (RA) sits on the mount. The one who is Mu‘adh’s teacher is now walking beside his mount. And that statement, perhaps we will not meet again. Mu‘adh (RA)’s eyes overflowed. Then the Prophet {{1}}, turning toward Madinah, said, the people closest to me are the muttaqin, wherever they are. Consolation in answer to the weeping of separation, in the same scene.
blocks.35: And one more day, holding Mu‘adh’s hand. Mu‘adh (RA) says,
blocks.36: The Messenger of Allah {{1}} took his hand and said, O Mu‘adh, by Allah, I love you. By Allah, I love you. Then he said, I advise you, Mu‘adh, do not fail to say this at the end of every prayer: Allahumma a‘inni ‘ala dhikrika, wa-shukrika, wa-husni ‘ibadatik. (O Allah, help me in remembering You, in thanking You, and in worshipping You well.){{2}}
blocks.37: A declaration of love, then a small supplication. What he gave a dear student in the last months of his life was no treasure. A sentence at the end of prayer. How much we store up words for love. A sentence worth saying, a supplication worth making, how easy it was.
blocks.39: Eight years have passed since Uhud. One day the Prophet {{1}} went to the graves of the martyrs of that battle. ‘Uqbah ibn ‘Amir (RA) says,
blocks.40: The Messenger of Allah {{1}} prayed the funeral prayer for the martyrs of Uhud after eight years, as though bidding farewell to the living and the dead. Then he ascended the pulpit and said, I am going ahead of you, and I am a witness over you. The place of my meeting with you is the Hawd. I can see it from this place of mine. I do not fear that you will commit shirk. But my fear is that you will fall to competing with one another over the world. ‘Uqbah (RA) says, that was my last sight of the Messenger of Allah {{2}}.{{3}}
blocks.41: Coming beside the graves of the martyrs after eight years he said, I am going ahead of you, I am a witness over you. The matter of testimony on the Day of Resurrection he stated in advance. And the matter of fear. Not shirk, but competition over the world. For the generation that has broken the idols he did not think of shirk. He thought of wealth, of power, of the race of overtaking one another. What is our fear about? Competition with others, getting a little more, arriving a little earlier. The fear he spoke of in the last days is exactly our daily race.
blocks.43: The graveyard of Madinah, al-Baqi‘. One night the Prophet {{1}} went there quietly, waking no one. ‘A’ishah (RA) followed him that night. Later she asked why. The Prophet {{2}} said,
blocks.44: Jibril came to me, when you saw me. He called me, concealing it from you; and I answered, concealing it from you. I thought you had fallen asleep, so I did not want to wake you, and I feared you would be left alone. He said, your Lord commands you to go to the people of al-Baqi‘ and ask forgiveness for them.{{1}}
blocks.45: And what would he say to those of the graves? He taught ‘A’ishah (RA),
blocks.46: Say: peace upon the dwellers of these houses, the believers and Muslims. May Allah have mercy on those of us who went ahead and those who will come later. And, if Allah wills, we will join you.{{1}}
blocks.47: The last sentence, we will join you. Standing beside a grave he himself speaks of his own journey, in a simple tone. No fear, no resentment. Only salaam and supplication. A silent journey of one night at Allah’s command. A command to ask forgiveness for those who have died. We walk past graveyards. We never stop to make supplication.
blocks.49: One more task of putting in order remained. The battle of Mu’tah on the Syrian border, where Zayd ibn Harithah (RA) was martyred (Dars 21). Now another army to that border. The commander Zayd’s son Usamah. Ibn ‘Umar (RA) says,
blocks.50: The Messenger of Allah {{1}} sent an army, and made Usamah ibn Zayd its commander. Some people spoke about his leadership. The Messenger of Allah {{2}} stood and said, if you speak about his leadership, you had spoken before about his father’s leadership too. By Allah, he was fit for leadership. He was among the dearest of people to me. And this one (Usamah) after him is among the dearest of people to me.{{3}}
blocks.51: Father Zayd, son Usamah. At Mu’tah the father was martyred. Now in that father’s place his son, the commander. Young in age, so talk arose too. The Prophet {{1}} stood up. He said, you said this very thing about the father too. By Allah, he was fit. And this son is fit too. He who is preparing to go is also finishing the preparation for the battlefield. That after him no task remain unfinished. He listened to the Companions’ talk too, but did not move from the decision on fitness. In today’s leadership how easily we measure fitness by age, lineage, relationship.
blocks.53: In the part on the Farewell Hajj and the last preparations there are some more narrations that people often tell. They too have been kept here. The chain and grade of each is given in the footnote. There is a famous narration about the supplication of the day of ‘Arafah. ‘Amr ibn Shu‘ayb narrates from his father and grandfather, the Prophet {{1}} said,
blocks.54: The best supplication is the supplication of the day of ‘Arafah. And the best of what I and the prophets before me have said is, there is no god but Allah, He is One, He has no partner, His is the kingdom, His is the praise, and He has power over all things.{{1}}
blocks.55: The best supplication of the day of ‘Arafah is this sentence of tawhid. There is a detailed narration of the Prophet’s {{1}} going to the graveyard of al-Baqi‘ before his last illness, in which the matter of the choice is also mentioned. His freed slave Abu Muwayhibah (RA) says,
blocks.56: The Prophet {{1}} said, O Abu Muwayhibah, I have been commanded to ask forgiveness for these people of al-Baqi‘. Come with me. I went. Standing among them he said, peace upon you, O people of the graves. May this state of yours be blessed for you, compared to the state people are in. Trials are advancing like pieces of a dark night, one after another, and the last worse than the first. Then, turning his face to me, he said, O Abu Muwayhibah, I have been given the keys of the treasures of the world, and eternal life there, then Paradise. I have been given the choice between this and meeting my Lord and Paradise. I said, may my parents be sacrificed for you, take the keys of the world’s treasures and everlasting life, then Paradise. He said, no, by Allah, O Abu Muwayhibah, I have chosen the meeting with my Lord and Paradise. Then he asked forgiveness for the people of al-Baqi‘, and returned. When it was morning that illness of his began, in which Allah took him.{{2}}
blocks.57: There are a few more narrations, about which a brief word can be said.{{1}}
blocks.59: The Hajj after nine years. Nine counted on Jabir’s fingers, then before countless eyes a man. A pilgrim riding a worn saddle. Asma’s new child, ‘Ali’s anger, Suraqah’s question. Crossing the line of Quraysh’s pride to ‘Arafah with everyone. The verse of the Qur’an, today the religion is complete. After sunset the pull of the rein, a hand on al-Fadl’s face. With his own hand sixty-three camels, the shared hair, one sip from the bucket of Zamzam. On the day of sacrifice three silences, then the duty of conveying. At the pond of Khumm one sentence in ‘Ali’s favour. And the hints. Perhaps there will be no more Hajj. The Qur’an twice, twenty days of i‘tikaf. Mu‘adh’s weeping, the last sight at the martyrs of Uhud, asking forgiveness on the night of al-Baqi‘. The banner in Usamah’s hand. In every picture a man, and he is not speaking of himself. He is speaking of women’s rights, the paying of debts, a brother’s wealth, the Book of Allah, what will you say about me. Before going, he is putting the ummah in order. The Qur’an has described this man this way,
blocks.61: (O people!) There has come to you a Messenger from among yourselves. Any hardship of yours is very grievous to him. He is ever solicitous for your good, extremely kind to the believers, most merciful.{{1}}
blocks.62: The man to whom any hardship of ours was heavy did not speak of his own hardship even in the last days. He spoke of us. So take one task from today’s dars.
blocks.64: In the Farewell Hajj the Prophet {{1}} began the reform from his own house: first of all abolishing the blood claim of his own clan and the usury dues of his own uncle, and he said, debts must be paid. Today I will ask myself one question, what is still owed to me by whom, and what dues can I give up to whom? Today I will pay one debt, or give up one due, and from today I will never give up keeping this account of debt and trust.

footnotes.0: Sahih Muslim 2408 (from Zayd ibn Arqam (RA), through Yazid ibn Hayyan; sahih). ‘Thaqalayn’ = two weighty (precious) things. The place of the incident is ‘Khumm’, between Makkah and Madinah (the wording of the hadith).
footnotes.1: Sahih Muslim 2408 (from Zayd ibn Arqam (RA); sahih). In the narration ‘udhakkirukumu Allaha fi ahli bayti’ three times.
footnotes.2: Sahih Muslim 2408 (from Zayd ibn Arqam (RA); sahih). The narrator Zayd himself explained the scope of ‘Ahl al-Bayt’: the wives are within the household, but the Ahl al-Bayt addressed by this counsel are those for whom sadaqah is forbidden (these four families of Banu Hashim).
footnotes.3: Sahih al-Bukhari 4350 (from Buraydah ibn al-Husayb (RA), through his son ‘Abdullah; sahih). In al-Bukhari at the beginning of the narration: the Prophet {{1}} had sent ‘Ali to Khalid to bring the khums, and Buraydah disliked ‘Ali (the details of the reason are not there, so the narration says ‘resentment over the khums’, which is consistent with the narration).
footnotes.4: Musnad Ahmad 22945, from Buraydah ibn al-Husayb al-Aslami (RA). In the edition edited by Shu‘ayb Arna’ut 23057: ‘the chain is sahih on the condition of al-Bukhari and Muslim’; Ibn Hibban 6930 (sahih); Ibn Kathir, al-Bidayah wa al-Nihayah 5/184: ‘the chain is jayyid qawi, all narrators thiqah’. In another narration the wording ‘man kuntu waliyyahu fa-‘Aliyyun waliyyuhu’ (Arna’ut 23057). ‘Wali/mawla’: friend, helper, beloved.
footnotes.5: Musnad Ahmad 18479 (from al-Bara’ ibn ‘Azib (RA), through ‘Adi ibn Thabit). Shu‘ayb Arna’ut: ‘sahih li-ghayrihi’ (18479, 18480). Jami‘ al-Tirmidhi 3713 (from Zayd ibn Arqam or Abu Sarihah (RA); ‘hasan sahih’): ‘man kuntu mawlahu fa-‘Aliyyun mawlahu’. In the same narration after this come ‘Allahumma wali man walahu wa-‘adi man ‘adahu’ (O Allah, be a friend to whoever befriends ‘Ali, be an enemy to whoever is hostile to him) and also ‘Umar (RA)’s congratulation. There is disagreement among scholars about those parts (Imam Ahmad and al-‘Uqayli called some routes weak; Ibn al-‘Arabi, ‘Aridat al-Ahwadhi 7/159: ‘weak’). So only the first part is quoted. Time of the incident: near the pond of ‘Khumm’, on the way back from Hajj (Sahih Muslim 2408); al-Rahiq al-Makhtum does not mention this incident.
footnotes.6: There is scholarly disagreement over the meaning of the word ‘mawla’ and the significance of this announcement. The scholars of Ahl al-Sunnah have understood this announcement as a declaration of love, friendship and support for ‘Ali; its background is Buraydah’s complaint (Bukhari 4350; Ahmad 22945). Another view (Shi‘ah) is that it is the designation of ‘Ali’s caliphate. Here, with sources, the basis of the Ahl al-Sunnah understanding is given: the background (the incident of Buraydah), the use of the word ‘wali’ (Ahmad 23057, Arna’ut), and the Companions’ later conduct even after this announcement (Abu Bakr’s pledge at Saqifah, which is in Dars 26). The detail of the theoretical debate is outside the boundary of this dars.
footnotes.7: Tawdih al-Qur’an, vol. 3, Surah al-Nasr 110:1–3, p. 755 (matched by reading the printed page in Dars 22). Arabic: Al-Qur’an Cloud (Uthmani script). Ibn ‘Umar’s narration on the place and time of the surah’s revelation (at Mina, at the Farewell Hajj) is ‘very weak’ (Ibn Rajab, Tafsir Surat al-Nasr 2/514: ‘the chain is very weak’; Musa ibn ‘Ubaydah). So the narration does not state the place and time of revelation.
footnotes.8: Sahih al-Bukhari 4970 (from Ibn ‘Abbas (RA), through Sa‘id ibn Jubayr; sahih).
